title: Hosted API traffic-tier decomposition PRD and staged launch checklist
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines an approach to decompose the Hosted API surface by traffic tiers and endpoint behavior (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) and the staged launch checklist required to bring the unified surface to GA. The goal is to provide a small, well-scoped v1 that meets production SLOs and a predictable cost envelope for customers, while leaving clear hooks to enable higher-cost quality bands and tenant-specific Dedicated/private rollouts later.

Scope for v1 (must-haves):
- Single HTTP/JSON surface supporting chat and completions generation and an embeddings endpoint and a rerank endpoint.
- Behavioral contracts (response shape, streaming semantics for chat/completions, deterministic rerank seed behavior) documented and enforced.
- Telemetry and dashboards: token-level cost, 95/99th latency, error rates by model lane, per-route cost breakdown.
- Canary rollout plan and automated rollback triggers tied to quality regression signals.
- Autoscaling policies for hosted capacity with tenant-aware burst protections.

Out of scope for v1 (explicitly deferred):
- Multi-protocol (gRPC) surface (deferred to v2).
- Per-tenant private model hosting and Dedicated billing contracts (handled by Dedicated/Private streams).
- Complex multi-stage quality profiles (will add after GA).

Background and motivation:
Customers want a predictable and simple hosted surface that is safe for product teams to adopt. Historically we shipped many features together and some launches slipped because of unclear acceptance criteria for quality vs cost. This ticket decomposes the launch requirements by traffic tier (fast/low-cost vs high-quality) and by endpoint so PM, Eng, and Design can agree on minimal behavioral guarantees for GA while leaving advanced options for later increments.
acceptance_criteria: General: public API contract documented in Confluence + OpenAPI snippet; breaking changes require version bump; all public endpoints return stable shape keys for Response/Meta fields.
General: infra can sustain sustained throughput of 1000 rps at small payloads for the low-cost traffic tier in our primary region with 95th percentile latency targets met (see per-endpoint targets).

Chat (generation): streaming responses supported; 95th percentile tail <= 250ms for short prompts (<256 tokens) on low-cost lane; deterministic function/tool-call schema for function-calling contracts; tooling for per-prompt metadata (prompt_id, eval_id) included in response headers.

Completions: batch inference semantics stabilized for sync calls; top_k/top_p and temperature control exposed; 95th percentile latency <= 200ms for short prompts on low-cost lane; generation seeds optional for deterministic replay in evals.

Embeddings: output vector shape stable (vec_length declared in OpenAPI); embedding consistency test suite (cosine-distance regression harness) passes on candidate models vs baseline; end-to-end latency 95th <= 120ms for single-item requests in low-cost tier.

Rerank: stable ranking contract for same input+seed; top-10 recall and ordering stability tests pass; reranker returns scores and normalized ranking metadata; 95th latency <= 180ms for typical workload in low-cost lane.

Telemetry & Observability: per-route dashboards exist (tokens, cost per 1k tokens, p50/p95/p99 latency, error_breakdown), and alerts tied to anomalies with runbook links; all endpoints emit tracing hooks compatible with Console tracing integration.

Rollout Safety: canary slice at 1% with automated rollback on either (1) latency regression >20% p95 vs baseline, (2) error rate >0.5% absolute increase, or (3) evaluation quality regressions flagged by the eval harness for a sampled prompt-set.

Security & Compliance: SSO for console access verified; KMS integration tested for any customer-managed keys referenced by hosted logs; security review checklist completed prior to GA (see security_review_required flag).

scope_changes_and_decisions: 2026-03-04: Removed request-level batching API from v1 (decision): batching will be handled within the runtime via adaptive continuous batching; a public batch endpoint adds compatibility surface that we cannot reliably meet for GA. Trade-off: simpler API and faster launch vs some customer's desire for explicit batch endpoints.
2026-03-06: Deferred multi-protocol support (gRPC) to v2 to reduce initial test matrix and allow focused QA on JSON/HTTP surface.
2026-03-09: Scoped embeddings to a single declared vector size set per model in catalog rather than a negotiation protocol; this avoids complexity for v1 but requires clearer model catalog docs.

2026-03-10: Seed-determinism for rerank included as optional query param; determinism required for eval-run replayability but disabled by default for low-cost lane to preserve performance and caching benefits.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Quality regressions during canary could impact active customers. Mitigation: 1% canary, automatic rollback on quality and latency signals, and an eval harness sampling customer prompt-sets prior to canary.
Risk: Cost overrun if low-cost lane traffic exceeds capacity. Mitigation: tenant-aware rate limiting with graceful degrade to fallback model variant and cost alerts to PM/Revenue Ops.
Risk: Telemetry gaps under high throughput. Mitigation: synthetic traffic runs during soak tests and sampling rate adjustments for high-volume tenants.
launch_checklist: Pre-launch signoffs: PM, Eng lead, Security, SRE, Observability - all documented in Confluence.
QA: End-to-end integration tests including streaming, function calling, and rerank ordering smoke tests passed in staging.
Ops: Autoscaling policies verified under synthetic surge tests; burst protections confirmed for tenant isolation.
Telemetry: Dashboards live and alerting thresholds configured with runbook links (CPU, token cost, p95 latency, error rate, eval-score drift).
Canary: Release to 1% internal+external traffic for 24 hours with daily eval snapshots; if stable, ramp to 10% for 48 hours before GA.
Documentation: Public API reference, migration guide, and quickstart sample code snippets published and linked from Console onboarding flow.
Support: Customer success & SE playbook with escalation paths and cost-exposure visibility ready for first ten onboarded customers.
Rollback: Verified rollback procedure and automated feature toggle to disable new host surface; manual rollback drill completed by SRE team.
decision_log: 2026-03-04: Adaptive runtime batching favored over explicit batch API for v1 (Maya P., Liam O.).
2026-03-06: gRPC deferred to v2 to reduce scope (PM + Eng alignment).
2026-03-09: Embedding vector size fixed per model in catalog for GA to avoid negotiation complexity.
